accepted.question_text: Fix a positive integer k. Are there only finitely many integer quadruples (x, y, p, q) with x, y, p, q >= 2 such that x^p - y^q = k?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.3 (Pillai). Let k be a positive integer. The equation x^p - y^q = k, where the unknowns x, y, p and q take integer values, all >= 2, has only finitely many solutions (x, y, p, q).

accepted.question_text: Given k consecutive composite integers n + 1, ..., n + k, must there exist k distinct primes p_1, ..., p_k such that p_j divides n + j for each 1 <= j <= k?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.6 (Grimm). Given k consecutive composite integers n + 1, . . . , n + k, there exist k distinct primes p1 , . . . , pk such that n + j is divisible by pj , 1 <= j <= k.

accepted.question_text: If n_1 < ... < n_k are positive integers that are multiplicatively dependent, must there be at least one prime in the interval [n_1, n_k]?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.8 (Langevin). Given an increasing sequence n1 < n2 < · · · < nk of positive integers such that n1 , n2 , . . . , nk are multiplicatively dependent, there exists a prime number in the interval [n1 , nk ].

accepted.question_text: For every epsilon > 0, does there exist a constant kappa(epsilon) such that whenever a, b, c are pairwise coprime positive integers with a + b = c, one has c < kappa(epsilon) R(abc)^(1 + epsilon)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1 (abc Conjecture). For each ε > 0 there exists a positive number κ(ε) which has the following property: if a, b and c are three positive rational integers which are relatively prime and satisfy a + b = c, then c < κ(ε)R(abc)1+ε .

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an integer k such that if two positive integers m and n satisfy R(m + i) = R(n + i) for every i = 0, ..., k - 1, then m = n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2 (Erdős-Woods). There exists a positive integer k such that, for m and n positive integers, the conditions R(m + i) = R(n + i) (i = 0, . . . , k − 1) imply m = n.

accepted.question_text: If positive integers a < b have the same radical R(a) = R(b), must there be a prime p with a < p < b?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.3 (Erdős–Dressler). If a and b are two positive integers with a < b and R(a) = R(b) then there is a prime p with a < p < b.

accepted.question_text: If x and y are positive integers with y^2 != x^3, is it always true that |y^2 - x^3| >= C max(y^2, x^3)^(1/6) for some absolute constant C > 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.7 (Hall). If x and y are positive integers with y 2 6= x3 , then |y 2 − x3 | ≥ C max{y 2 , x3 }1/6 .

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a nonzero real number alpha such that, for every positive integer n, the fractional part of alpha (3/2)^n lies in [0, 1/2)?

evidence.quote: K. Mahler defined a Z-number as a nonzero real number α such that the fractional part rn of α(3/2)n satisfies 0 ≤ rn < 1/2 for any positive integer n. It is not known whether Z-numbers exist.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove that the fractional part of e^n does not tend to 0 as n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: We are not yet able to prove that the fractional part of e^n does not tend to 0 as n tends to infinity.

accepted.question_text: Given positive integers k_1, ..., k_n, does there exist a real number x such that ||k_i x|| >= 1/(n+1) for every i = 1, ..., n?

evidence.quote: There are several open questions known as “view obstruction Problems”. One of them is the following. Given n positive integers k1 , . . . , kn , there exists a real number x such that ||ki x|| ≥ 1/(n + 1) for 1 ≤ i ≤ n.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove the irrationality of Euler’s constant gamma, Catalan’s constant G, or Gamma(1/5)? More generally, can one decide whether numbers such as e + pi, e^gamma, zeta(5), and zeta(3)/pi^3 are irrational, algebraic, or transcendental?

evidence.quote: No proof of irrationality has been given so far for Euler’s constant ... nor for Catalan’s constant ... nor for Γ(1/5) ... or for numbers like e + π, eγ, ζ(5), ζ(3)/π 3.

accepted.question_text: If x_1, ..., x_n are linearly independent over Q, must the field Q(x_1, ..., x_n, e^{x_1}, ..., e^{x_n}) have transcendence degree at least n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 (Schanuel). Let x1 , . . . , xn be Q-linearly independent complex numbers. Then the transcendence degree over Q of the field Q(x1 , . . . , xn , e^{x1} , . . . , e^{xn}) is at least n.

accepted.question_text: If lambda_1, ..., lambda_n are linearly independent over Q and e^{lambda_1}, ..., e^{lambda_n} are algebraic, must lambda_1, ..., lambda_n be algebraically independent over Q?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3 (Algebraic Independence of Logarithms of Algebraic Numbers). Let λ1 , . . . , λn be Q-linearly independent complex numbers. Assume that the numbers e^{λ1} , . . . , e^{λn} are algebraic. Then the numbers λ1 , . . . , λn are algebraically independent over Q.

accepted.question_text: If x_1, x_2 are linearly independent over Q and y_1, y_2 are linearly independent over Q, must at least one of exp(x_i y_j) for i, j in {1, 2} be transcendental?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.7 (Four Exponentials Conjecture). Let x1 , x2 be two Q-linearly independent complex numbers and y1 , y2 also two Q-linearly independent complex numbers. Then at least one of the four numbers exp(xi yj ) (i = 1, 2, j = 1, 2) is transcendental.

accepted.question_text: Are the numbers pi, zeta(3), zeta(5), zeta(7), ... algebraically independent over Q?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.17. The numbers π, ζ(3), ζ(5), . . . , ζ(2n + 1), . . . are algebraically independent over Q.

accepted.question_text: If an irreducible subvariety Z of A_g(C) contains a Zariski-dense set of complex multiplication points, must Z be of Hodge type?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.22 (André–Oort). Let Ag (C) denote the moduli space of principally polarized complex abelian varieties of dimension g. Let Z be an irreducible algebraic subvariety of Ag (C) such that the complex multiplication points on Z are dense for the Zariski topology. Then Z is a subvariety of Ag (C) of Hodge type.

accepted.question_text: Are there transcendental entire functions f such that every Liouville number x is sent to another Liouville number f(x)?

evidence.quote: Question 3.27 (Mahler). Are there entire transcendental functions f (z) such that if x is a Liouville number then so is f (x)?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.6. For θ ∈ (0, π), define Vθ = {reit ; r > 0, |t| > θ}. Compute L(Vθ ) in terms of θ.

evidence.quote: Question 4.17 (Mazur). Assume that K = Q and that V (Q) is Zariski dense; is Z a union of connected components of V (R)?

accepted.question_text: For n >= 2, describe the set of real numbers xi such that there are constants c_1(xi), c_2(xi) > 0 with uniform lower bounds for approximation by algebraic numbers of degree at most n, while infinitely many algebraic numbers of degree exactly n achieve the corresponding Dirichlet-type upper bound.

evidence.quote: Question 5.2 (Bugeaud). Let n ≥ 2. Denote by Жn the set of real numbers ξ with the following property: there exists c1 (ξ) > 0 and c2 (ξ) > 0 such that for algebraic number α of degree ≤ n, |ξ − α| ≥ c2 (ξ)H(α)−n−1 , and such that there are infinitely many algebraic numbers α of degree exactly n with |ξ − α| ≤ c1 (ξ)H(α)−n−1 .

accepted.question_text: Let (n_i) be an increasing sequence of positive integers, and suppose there is a prime p such that the power series sum z^{n_i} in F_p[[z]] is algebraic over F_p(z). Must the real number sum 10^{-n_i} be either rational or transcendental?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.4 (Loxton and van der Poorten). Let (ni )i≥0 be an increasing sequence of positive integers. Assume there is a prime number p such that the power series sum z^{ni} in Fp [[z]] is algebraic over Fp (z). Then the real number sum 10^{-ni} is either rational or transcendental.
